name: Mahathir Mohamad
summary: A Malay nationalist and developmental statist who ran Malaysia for 22 years with state-led industrialisation, privatisation, Bumiputera preferences and tight security and press laws, then returned in 2018 on an anti-corruption platform. Abroad he attacked Western dominance of the UN, trade rules and finance, defended developing countries' right to develop first and championed the Palestinian cause.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: In 2019 he said states can negotiate or submit to third-party arbitration or the ICJ, and that Malaysia settled disputes with neighbours that way.

arms-reduction.rationale: In 1991 he said the existence of any nuclear weapons cannot be justified and that weapons are needed only against criminals.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: After Anwar's December 1997 spending cut failed, Mahathir and Daim reflated the economy through lower interest rates, credit expansion and a stimulus package.

ban-cartels.rationale: In 2019 he warned that a person or company with so much money can buy power, and said this is why anti-trust laws are needed.

capital-controls.rationale: In September 1998 he imposed sweeping capital-account controls and pegged the ringgit at 3.80 to the dollar.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: In 2018 he said states dropping bombs that maim and kill innocent people commit acts of terrorism and that killing in war is wrongly glorified.

class-collaboration.rationale: His Look East policy promoted in-house unions that cooperate with management for productivity, over industry-wide unions.

close-ties-china.rationale: In 2018 he suspended China-financed rail and pipeline projects over cost, yet later reopened talks on them and said Malaysia is friend to all.

conscription.rationale: His government passed the National Service Training Act 2003, which makes registration and attendance compulsory and punishes failure with fines or jail.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: In 1995 he said environmental sustainability, social equity and fulfilment of human needs must replace the culture of materialism.

corporate-influence.rationale: He said in 2019 that huge corporate wealth can influence things and buy power, and attacked big companies' terms in the Trans-Pacific Partnership.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He framed the Shared Prosperity Vision as a way to bring Bumiputera equity ownership to 30 per cent and give neglected groups a fair share.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: His government charged Anwar with 'unnatural sex' in 1998, applying the criminal law on same-sex relations.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: As prime minister-elect he said the GST on goods and services would be cancelled and the earlier sales tax restored.

death-penalty.rationale: He enforced the mandatory death penalty for drug trafficking through 22 years, but his 2018 government announced abolition and imposed an execution moratorium.

delink-world-market.rationale: In 2003 he said Malaysia's population is too small for a domestic market so it needs the world market, and asked partners not to restrict its exports.

democracy-best.rationale: In 2019 he said democracy is a better form of government than dictatorship, while stressing it is hard to operate and needs gradual adoption.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: In 1993 he called his country's multiracial make-up a time bomb inherited from its colonial past.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He signed the ISA detention orders of 1987 and said he would arrest the same people again under the same situation.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: In 1991 he urged giving the UN comprehensive authority over disarmament and arms supervision, and in 2019 said the UN is worth supporting.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: His government kept Bumiputera preferences throughout and in 2018 shelved ICERD ratification over Article 153, then launched a plan raising Bumiputera equity to 30 per cent.

every-country-ready-for-democracy.rationale: In 2019 he argued that an overnight switch to democracy brings destabilisation and civil war, and that time should be allowed for a gradual transition.

free-trade.rationale: His government protected Proton with tariffs of up to 300 percent, a record of shielding domestic industry rather than free trade.

future-generations.rationale: In 1995 he said economic development should not be at the expense of other groups or future generations.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: In 2003 he said he had a feeling that the disasters are part of cycles of change that the planet has gone through for millions of years.

independent-unions.rationale: The registrar's refusal to register the electronics workers' union was found by the ILO committee to breach Convention 98, yet the government did not change course.

industrial-unions.rationale: His government favoured enterprise-level house unions and the Registrar refused to register the industry-wide Electrical Industry Workers Union.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: In 1999 he objected that the West insists there is only one way of administering a country, the liberal democratic way, and in 1991 asked who may interpret democracy.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: He called it ridiculous to hang one murderer yet glorify those responsible for millions of deaths, and proposed criminalising war.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He has repeatedly said Israel was created by seizing Palestinian land, accepting it in 2019 only as a fait accompli.

legalize-drugs.rationale: In 1983 his government made death mandatory for possessing over 15 grams of heroin, and he refused clemency appeals with the answer 'tell that to the drug traffickers'.

limit-growth.rationale: In 1995 he said forcing developing countries to stay undeveloped to preserve the environment for the rich is manifestly unfair.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: His record mixes privatisation with state-led heavy industry, tariff protection and the 1998 capital controls, so it points both ways.

minority-language-support.rationale: His government gave Chinese and Tamil schools land and aid, and a 1996 Education Act amendment removed the minister's power to close them.

multipolar-world.rationale: In 2003 he said a unipolar world dominated by one democratic nation leads the world into economic chaos and political anarchy.

national-self-determination.rationale: In 1991 he welcomed the Baltic states' regained sovereignty and in 1996 spoke for Chechnya's valiant people against Russia.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: In 2019 he called talk of never giving up an inch of territory ridiculous and urged courts and negotiation over war.

party-controls-media.rationale: Three newspapers were suspended in 1987 and pro-Anwar editors were forced to resign and broadcast signals jammed in 1998.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: He told the General Assembly in 2019 that Muslim countries had been destabilised by the campaign for democracy and regime change.

public-ownership.rationale: His 1983 privatisation policy moved state enterprises such as utilities, airlines and telecoms into private hands.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Instead of going to the IMF he imposed controls, cut interest rates and reflated in 1998, rejecting an IMF-style adjustment programme.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: At the 2003 OIC summit he said scholars' interpretations are not prophets' and that Muslims had interpreted the religion wrongly, though he urged a return to fundamentals.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: In his 2003 General Assembly speech he proposed a UN levy on world trade for poor-country infrastructure, a ban on rich-country subsidies and temporary protection for poor countries' industries.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He told the UN in 2018 that freedom had led to the negation of marriage and families, and said in September 2018 that Malaysia cannot accept LGBT culture.

separate-church-state.rationale: He has said Malaysia is an ordinary state that recognises Islam as official religion and was never declared secular.

separated-powers.rationale: A panel found the 1988 sacking of the Lord President, who upheld separation of powers, and two judges unconstitutional; the tribunals came under his government, though he denies responsibility.

single-official-language.rationale: He said Malaysia, unlike other countries, allows mother-tongue languages to be used and taught in its schools.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He chose the car industry and founded Proton through the state's heavy-industries corporation HICOM, a state-led push into a strategic industry.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: His 2018 UN speech said the new Malaysia remains neutral and non-aligned, a friend to all and an enemy to none.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His government jailed opposition leaders and suspended newspapers in Operation Lalang (1987) and arrested Anwar's supporters and banned reformasi meetings in 1998; in 2018 he pledged repeals and prosecutors dropped some sedition cases.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: His national car project shielded Proton behind import duties of up to 300 percent on foreign cars, and he restated the infant-industry case in later UN speeches.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: He said environmental standards were for developing countries alone to judge and objected to rich countries scrutinising human-rights records to withdraw trade preferences.

traditional-family.rationale: In 2018 he lamented that freedom had negated the concept of marriage and families and moral codes.

war-builds-character.rationale: In 2018 and 2019 he called war primitive and said killing a million is wrongly rewarded with heroes' medals and statues.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: In 2003 he called the World Bank, IMF and WTO instruments of hegemony that impoverish the poor and enrich the rich.

notes: Position changes: in his second term (2018-2020) he pledged to repeal the Sedition Act, Printing Presses Act and mandatory death sentences and announced a death penalty moratorium, but this lasted under two years and mostly stayed pledges, so the death penalty is recorded as mixed and the earlier security record stands on suppression. Themes searched: economy (privatisation, industrial policy, 1998 crisis response, taxes), government (ISA, press, judiciary, Anwar), society (Bumiputera policy, family, LGBT), world (UN, Israel, trade, arms, intervention, China), ecology (Rio 1992, forests, climate). Not available: the full text of The Malay Dilemma (archive.org lending only) and Malaysia's parliamentary record, so his positions on race and heredity, elections, courts, women, language and welfare were left null. The Anwar and other ISA arrests are attributed to the government where the sources do not name him personally.
